qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: The debate team praised the federalism between its two captains, who split the speaking time evenly and traded the closing argument round by round.
Under the republic's federalism, the provinces run their own schools and police while the national government keeps the currency and the army.
The ministry's federalism was absolute: every bell time, syllabus, and school lunch in the country was set by clerks in the capital, three time zones from most classrooms.
The two kingdoms signed a treaty of federalism, each pledging to defend the other's borders in any future war.

qti-content-body.p: Correct! Federalism means a constitutional division of power between a national government and the country's regions, so it's the correct answer because the provinces hold schools and police in their own right while the national government keeps the currency and the army — two levels, each supreme in its own sphere.

Not quite. Federalism is a term of art: it names one specific constitutional arrangement, and the test is where governing power sits and who holds it by right. Re-read the card's definition and ask of each sentence: is governing power genuinely divided here, and between whom?

Not quite! Federalism means a constitutional division of power between a national government and its regions, so it's not the correct choice here because two debate captains splitting speaking time is simple teamwork — no governments, no constitution, no levels of power anywhere in the sentence.

Not quite! Federalism means power constitutionally divided between a national government and its regions, so it's not the correct choice here because this ministry has gathered every school decision into the capital — that is centralization, the arrangement federalism exists to divide up.

Not quite! Federalism means one country's constitution dividing power between its national government and its regions, so it's not the correct choice here because two separate kingdoms promising mutual defense have formed an alliance between sovereign countries, not levels of government within one.
